nodes.name: When Executed by Another Workflow
nodes.notes: Callable workflow input. Required: url. Optional aliases: targetUrl, sourceUrl, href, link. Redis rate limit fields are optional and default to the free Jina Reader no-key limit.

nodes.name: Increment Rate Counter
nodes.notes: Redis INCR happens before each Reader fetch attempt. Expire+TTL is enabled so every attempt resets the counter window TTL. Reselect local Redis credentials after import.

nodes.name: Jina Reader
nodes.notes: Free/no-key Reader path. Uses the same Reader URL construction pattern as the Brave search workflow: https://r.jina.ai/${url}.

nodes.name: Wait For Rate Limit Window
nodes.notes: On rate limit hit, wait remaining TTL plus buffer, then try the same Reader attempt again. This does not advance retry.currentAttempt because no Reader fetch was made.

parameters.content:
## Redis rate limit
This workflow requires an n8n **Redis** credential.

Default key: `jina_reader:free:rpm`
Default limit: `20` attempts per `60` seconds
Default wait on limit hit: `remaining TTL + 5s` = `65s`

The Redis increment runs **before** every Reader fetch attempt. The TTL is reset to 60 seconds on every attempt, whether the later Reader request succeeds or fails.

Rate-limit waits do **not** advance the Reader retry attempt counter because no HTTP fetch was made.

## Jina Reader callable workflow
Receives one URL from another workflow, normalizes it with string-only logic, rate-limits with Redis, retries Reader HTTP errors, calls the free Jina Reader endpoint, and returns normalized markdown content.

Preferred downstream key: `content`

Reader URL pattern mirrors the working Brave search workflow:
`https://r.jina.ai/${url}`

Retry default: `maxAttempts: 3`; first fetch is attempt 1.

nodes.name: Prepare Attempt State
nodes.notes: Normalizes retry attempt state before every Redis rate-limit check. Reader attempt number only advances after a Jina Reader HTTP error, not after rate-limit waits.

nodes.name: Handle Reader Error
nodes.notes: Captures the actual HTTP error, appends it to retry.errors, and decides whether another Reader fetch attempt is available.

nodes.name: Retry Available?
nodes.notes: True branch loops back for the next Reader attempt. False branch returns a normalized error response to the caller.
